parsed.explanation: The dominant, dossier-documented feature is a national statutory restroom ban by birth sex — a tier-1 universal-exposure measure reaching every trans visitor, enacted by the legislature, justified by framing trans people as harassment risks, and backed by no enforceable anti-discrimination or hate-crime protection (the 2017 repeal left none in force). Courts have not relieved facility exclusion; complaints cannot secure access. This alone holds the jurisdiction in the Elevated band despite no criminalisation of trans identity and no documented border/document friction. Offsetting evidence is real but partial: a landmark 17-year sentence against officers for torturing a trans woman (first such conviction, though ~20 years late), a court striking an anti-equality decree, improved health guidance and a conversion-therapy ban. Rising hate crimes with trans women most affected lacks denominator or period, so it is not weighed as magnitude. Net: comparable to a polite-society birth-sex-facility ban with functioning but slow recourse — mid-Elevated, not Reduced.
